prompts.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: precise side-profile reference photograph for sculpting and texturing an interactive Blender fish model. A single living fish, whole body and every fin visible, perfectly lateral side view, nose pointing RIGHT, tail LEFT, horizontally level. Plain dark charcoal aquarium-water background, no other animals, no plants, no rocks, no text, no labels. Frame the fish with generous empty margins, all fins uncropped. Photorealistic macro aquarium photography under neutral white diffused light: anatomically correct proportions, restrained natural highlights, tiny real scales, shallow natural eye, operculum and small mouth, fine translucent fin membranes and visible supporting rays. Avoid stylization, cartoon eyes, plastic surface, oversaturated flat colors, illustrative outlines, extra fins, duplicate fish, motion blur. True natural specimen quality; sharp focus across the fish. Subject: Paracanthurus hepatus, adult regal blue tang / palette surgeonfish. Deep laterally compressed oval cobalt-blue body, precise navy-black palette-shaped curved marking with blue oval window, yellow caudal fin bounded with black, small pointed snout, small dark eye set near the forehead, long low dorsal and anal fin profiles with fine dark edging, near-side yellow pectoral fin held close to the flank. Realistic subtle skin microtexture rather than oversized scales.

cleanFlankEditPrompt: Precise-object-edit for 3D texture authoring. Remove ONLY the near-side pectoral fin covering the side of this fish, filling that small area with anatomically plausible continuous matching body skin, fine scales and correct body color/markings. This clean flank will be used underneath a separately animated 3D pectoral fin. Preserve the exact pixel dimensions, crop, fish position, body silhouette, tail, all other fins, eye, mouth, gill cover, stripes, background, lighting and photographic quality. No new text, no labels. Do not shift, rotate, resize or redraw the fish. Only remove the single near-side pectoral fin, keep every other detail.
